name: Wellington International
desc: The showgrounds at the center of Wellington's winter season and home of the Winter Equestrian Festival. For thirteen weeks each winter, show jumpers, hunters and equitation riders from across the United States and dozens of countries compete here, and spectators can watch much of the action.
tips: The 2027 Winter Equestrian Festival runs January 6 to April 4
Saturday night grand prix events draw the biggest crowds
Plan for seasonal traffic on South Shore Blvd

name: National Polo Center
desc: The United States Polo Association's flagship venue, set on roughly 161 acres with seven tournament fields. Sunday polo during the winter season is a Wellington tradition, and the clubhouse hosts dining and private events.
tips: The 2026 to 2027 Palm Beach polo season runs December 27 to May 2
Sunday matches are the classic way to experience polo
Group seating is available for larger parties

name: Equestrian Village (Global Dressage Festival)
desc: The home of the Adequan Global Dressage Festival, which brings international dressage competition to Wellington each winter. Evening freestyle performances set to music are a highlight for spectators who are new to the sport.
tips: Dressage season typically runs January through March
Check the official schedule for evening freestyle nights

name: Peaceful Waters Sanctuary
desc: A roughly 30 acre wetland preserve tucked into the back of Village Park, with about 1,500 feet of elevated boardwalk and a one mile trail. It is one of the best free birdwatching spots in Palm Beach County, with herons, wading birds and the occasional alligator.
tips: Free admission and parking
Enter through Village Park and follow signs to the back lot
Dogs and bikes are not allowed on the trails

name: Village Park
desc: Wellington's largest park at about 114 acres, with athletic fields, two gymnasiums, a skate park, a playground and a walking path of roughly 2.5 miles. It is the hub for youth sports leagues across the village.
tips: Home to many youth league games on weekends
Peaceful Waters Sanctuary is at the back of the complex

name: Wellington Environmental Preserve
address: 3491 Flying Cow Ranch Rd, Wellington, FL 33414
desc: A 365 acre preserve at the Marjory Stoneman Douglas Everglades Habitat on the western edge of the village, with paved trails and a six story observation tower overlooking the Everglades landscape. Wide open and quiet, it is great for long walks and family bike rides.
tips: Bring water and sun protection, shade is limited
Climb the observation tower for the best views
Dogs are not permitted on the trails

name: Wellington Amphitheater
desc: The village's outdoor stage at Wellington Town Center, hosting concerts, movie nights, food truck events and seasonal festivals. Bring a blanket or lawn chair and make an evening of it by the lake.
tips: Many events are free to attend
Check the village events calendar for the current lineup

name: Wellington Town Center and Lake Wellington
desc: The civic heart of the village, set along Lake Wellington. Town Center brings together the amphitheater, community center, aquatics complex, Village Hall and Scott's Place, a popular playground designed so children of all abilities can play together.
tips: Scott's Place playground is a favorite for young kids
Walk the lakefront promenade at sunset

name: Wellington Aquatics Complex
desc: The village's public pool complex at Town Center, used for lap swimming, lessons, swim teams and summer fun. Resident rates are available.
tips: Check seasonal hours before you go
Swim lessons fill up quickly in spring

name: The Mall at Wellington Green
address: 10300 W Forest Hill Blvd, Wellington, FL 33414
desc: Wellington's regional shopping mall on State Road 7, with department stores, national retailers, restaurants and entertainment under one roof. The surrounding Wellington Green area is one of the busiest dining corridors in the village.
tips: Weekday mornings are the quietest time to shop
Several sit-down restaurants surround the mall

name: The Village Green
desc: A newer shopping and medical complex along State Road 7, anchored by Trader Joe's and a Cleveland Clinic facility, just east of the K-Park site where Village Landing is being built.
tips: Trader Joe's parking is busiest on weekend afternoons

name: Village Landing (coming 2028)
address: State Road 7 and Stribling Way, Wellington, FL 33414
desc: Related Ross is building Village Landing, a 71 acre walkable town center on the former K-Park land, with shops, restaurants, offices, a 180 room Hilton hotel and a central lake with a boardwalk. It is expected to open in fall 2028.
tips: Read our full guide to what is coming

name: Wingrove Academy (opening 2028)
desc: A new nonprofit PreK through 12 independent school being developed by ElevateED on the back portion of the K-Park site, with the first phase planned to open in August 2028.
tips: Read everything we know about the school

name: Lion Country Safari
address: 2003 Lion Country Safari Rd, Loxahatchee, FL 33470
desc: A drive-through safari park a short drive north of Wellington, where you tour animal habitats from your own car, then park for a walk-through area with rides, animal encounters and a water play zone. A classic day out for families.
tips: Arrive early on weekends to beat the line
Budget a full day if you plan to do the walk-through park

name: Okeeheelee Park
address: 7715 Forest Hill Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33413
desc: One of Palm Beach County's largest parks, just east of Wellington on Forest Hill Blvd, with lakes, trails, a nature center, a golf course and a BMX track.
tips: The nature center is a good stop for kids
Bring bikes for the paved trails

name: South Florida Fairgrounds and Yesteryear Village
address: 9067 Southern Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33411
desc: Home of the South Florida Fair each winter and events year round, plus Yesteryear Village, a living history park that recreates Florida life from the late 1800s to the mid 1900s.
tips: The South Florida Fair runs each January
Check the event calendar for weekend expos and shows

name: Mounts Botanical Garden
address: 531 N Military Trail, West Palm Beach, FL 33415
desc: Palm Beach County's oldest and largest public garden, with themed gardens, tropical fruit trees and a striking floating walkway over water.
tips: Go in the morning when it is cooler

name: Kaluz
desc: An upscale New American restaurant near Wellington Green with a full bar and outdoor seating, and one of the most talked about dinner spots in the village.

name: Agliolio Fresh Pasta and Wine Bar
desc: A family owned Italian spot known for fresh pasta and a lively, busy dining room. A local go-to for date nights and family dinners alike.

name: Hausmash
desc: A casual burger joint built around smashed burgers, fries and a laid-back atmosphere.

name: Spiro's Taverna of Wellington
desc: A Greek taverna that gave Wellington a sit-down option for gyros, grilled meats and Mediterranean classics.

name: Alacruz Grill Argentine Restaurant
desc: Argentine grill fare in a fine dining setting, a fitting cuisine for a town with deep ties to the polo world.

name: Rancho Argentino
desc: An Argentine restaurant serving grilled meats and traditional dishes.

name: Oli's Fashion Cuisine
desc: A longtime Wellington restaurant with a wide-ranging menu and a loyal local following.

name: Fujisan Asian Bistro
desc: A newer sushi and Asian bistro that quickly became a neighborhood favorite for rolls and gyoza.

name: Mochi Thai and Japanese
desc: Thai curries and noodle dishes alongside sushi, known for friendly, attentive service.

name: Kura Revolving Sushi Bar
desc: Conveyor belt sushi where plates come to you, a fun pick for kids and groups.

name: Cooper's Hawk Winery and Restaurant
desc: A restaurant and tasting room pairing a broad American menu with its own label wines.

name: Olive U Mediterranean Grill
desc: Fast, fresh Mediterranean plates and bowls with a strong following among locals.

name: Rosie's Pizza and Restaurant
desc: Neighborhood pizzeria and Italian kitchen with generous portions.

name: Sicilian Oven
desc: Coal and brick oven style pizza and Italian dishes, a reliable family dinner pick.

name: Emiliano Italian
desc: Italian dining for a sit-down dinner out.

name: Franco Italian Bistro
desc: An Italian bistro with a more upscale feel.

name: Talkin' Tacos
desc: Quick-serve tacos with late hours, popular for a casual bite.

name: Tulum Mexican Cuisine
desc: A sit-down Mexican restaurant that locals have rallied around since opening.

name: Keke's Breakfast Cafe
desc: Pancakes, omelets and brunch favorites. Expect a wait on weekend mornings.

name: Turning Point
desc: A bright breakfast and lunch spot for a healthier start to the day.

name: Kickback Neighborhood Tavern
desc: A neighborhood tavern for game nights, pub food and drinks with friends.
address: 12771 W Forest Hill Blvd, Wellington, FL 33414

name: Stonewood Grill and Tavern
desc: A classic American grill for steaks, seafood and a relaxed night out.

name: Bolay
desc: Build-your-own bowls with fresh, chef-driven ingredients, good for a quick healthy lunch.

name: Sushi Fans Cafe
desc: A casual neighborhood sushi spot on Wellington Trace.

name: SoBol
desc: Acai and fruit bowls, smoothies and a homemade almond butter that regulars rave about.

name: Whit's Frozen Custard
desc: Rich frozen custard with rotating flavors of the week, a summer evening ritual for Wellington families.

name: The Players Club
desc: A longtime gathering spot for the equestrian crowd near the showgrounds, busiest during the winter season.

name: JoJo's Raw Bar and Grill
desc: A casual neighborhood bar with oysters, daily specials and game nights, one of the places locals tend to bump into friends.

name: Kontiki Wine and Raw Bar
desc: A lively wine and raw bar with sushi, Asian-inspired plates and a busy bar scene.

name: Mallet Grill
desc: The grill at the National Polo Center, a natural stop before or after a Sunday match.

name: Rivales Taqueria and Craft Bar
desc: Tacos and craft cocktails in a date-night friendly setting.

name: Lindburgers
desc: A local burger spot with a big menu of creative burgers and outdoor seating.

name: Flanigan's
desc: The South Florida seafood, ribs and burgers institution, with a full bar.

name: Riptidez Kava Bar
desc: A late-night kava bar and social lounge, an alcohol-free alternative for a night out.

name: The Fresh Pita Club
desc: Homemade falafel, pitas and Mediterranean plates, with a following among falafel fans.

name: Chicken Salad Chick
desc: Chicken salads, sandwiches and sides, a quick and popular lunch stop.

name: Carmela Coffee
desc: Espresso drinks, breakfast sandwiches and pastries in a relaxed cafe.

name: Candid Coffee
desc: A friendly coffee shop known for protein coffees and specialty drinks.

name: Sushi Yama
desc: A small, popular sushi spot. They do not take reservations, so go early.

name: The Poke Company
desc: Build-your-own poke bowls with fresh fish and lots of toppings.

name: Sushi Moto Asian
desc: Sushi, curries and Asian dishes near the showgrounds, with a loyal local crowd.

name: Taylor Made Cafe
desc: A fresh, quick, owner-run cafe for healthy breakfasts and lunches.

name: Anna Bakes
desc: A neighborhood bakery for birthday treats, pastries and custom orders.

name: Christy's Bakery
desc: A local bakery best known for its cheesecakes and celebration cakes.

name: DeVine Bistro
desc: A polished bistro that is also a popular choice for private parties and celebrations.

name: Kabuki Sushi Thai Tapas
desc: A family-run spot for sushi, Thai dishes and small plates, welcoming to big groups.

name: Stallion
desc: An upscale New American restaurant with generous portions and live music some evenings.

name: Juan's Marketplace
desc: A cafe and marketplace with a devoted local following for casual dinners.

name: Maxwell's Plum
desc: A classic American restaurant and bar near the equestrian district.

name: Mole Cantina Mexicana
desc: Authentic Mexican dishes in a lively cantina atmosphere.

name: Jamaica House Grill
desc: Jamaican classics like jerk chicken and oxtail in a sit-down setting.

name: Park Avenue BBQ Grille
desc: A family barbecue restaurant with ribs, smoked meats and fast, friendly service.

name: Gabriel's Cafe and Grill
desc: A family-style diner for home fries, biscuits and gravy and classic breakfasts.

name: Short Stacks
desc: A longtime local breakfast spot, busy after Sunday services.

name: Casa Tequila
desc: A neighborhood Mexican restaurant and margarita spot.

name: La Granja
desc: Peruvian rotisserie chicken and Latin comfort food at casual prices.

name: Kobosko Kreamery
desc: A packed, cheerful ice cream shop with a huge flavor selection.

name: 3Natives
desc: Acai bowls, smoothies and wraps for a quick healthy bite.

name: China Hut
desc: Reliable Chinese takeout that happily customizes orders.

name: Panda Garden
desc: A friendly neighborhood Chinese restaurant for takeout and quick dinners.

name: First Watch
desc: Daytime breakfast, brunch and lunch with fresh juices.

name: Cilantro's Gourmet Deli
desc: A local deli for sandwiches and Latin-inspired lunches.

name: BurgerFi
desc: Better-burger chain with fries, shakes and a quick counter-service setup.

name: Lewis Prime Grill
desc: A Wellington grill that consistently ranks among the village's most popular dinner spots.

name: Boonies Wild West Saloon
desc: A country-style saloon just north of Wellington with live music and late hours.
